rows.en: He went to a fair in the next town

He skipped school and went to the next town.
It was festival season back then.
Okura wasn't the only one cutting class to go have fun there, either.
Me included, as a matter of fact.
The fair runs at night too, but having fun's no fun unless you break the rules a little, right?
Who I went with, I'll leave to your imagination.
Anyway, I was shocked when I spotted Okura.{p}

I thought about calling out to him, but his face was way too serious.
So I ended up following him.
Then he stops at one of the stalls.
A tiny stall selling garish plastic play-house toys and stuff like that.
He was haggling with the old man who ran it over something.{p}

Then the old man brought out a deck of cards.
They were bigger than playing cards, with flashy pictures on them.
"Those are tarot cards."
I didn't know that, but the person I was with said so.
The second Okura saw them, he reached out.
But the old man snatched them back before he could.
Okura looked like a dog that'd just been told to wait for its food.{p}

Okura spun around, startled...... then he saw it was me and smiled, all happy.
It was a weird smile.
Then he says he'll treat me if I come hang out with him.
I had nothing better to do anyway, so I figured why not.
But that smile from a second ago was bugging me, so I took another look at Okura.{p}
Without thinking, I shoved Okura away.{p}
"Aagh!"

Maybe he landed wrong, but the knife ended up stuck in Okura's gut.
Right then, a voice spoke up behind me.
"Oh my, oh my. You failed, didn't you?"
I turned around, and there was the old man from the stall.
He was looking down at Okura with a thin smirk.
"Still, a soul is a soul, no matter whose it is... It's more than enough to pay for these tarot cards."{p}

The old man waved the cards around like he was showing them off.
Okura was staring at them, bitter, but he didn't even have the strength left to reach out.
"Here I am, finally offering to sell, and you don't look like you'll be using them in that state.
What about your friend there?
How about a deck of tarot cards that'll do whatever you want?
Right now, I'll take Okura's soul in exchange."
The old man said that and looked at me.
Tarot cards you could make do whatever you wanted.
So Okura's playing cards had been the same kind of thing.{p}What would you do in a spot like that?
Refuse
Take the cards

Yeah, of course you would.
I turned him down too.
"I see. What a pity.
But it would be rude to take a soul for nothing, so I'll at least clear away Okura's body for you."
With that, the old man waved his hand.
At the same moment, Okura's body vanished.
And so did the old man.{p}

Okura ended up listed as missing.
I couldn't exactly tell anyone the truth.
I mean, I'm the one who killed him.
Who the old man really was?
...I think he might've been a devil.
Sound crazy?{p}Anyway, that's the end of my story.
Alright, time for the sixth one at last.{p}

Whoa, whoa, are you serious?
You look all meek, but you're actually a real piece of work, huh?
Even I hesitated there.
...Yeah, I turned him down.
"I see. What a pity.
But it would be rude to take a soul for nothing, so I'll at least clear away Okura's body for you."
With that, the old man waved his hand.
At the same moment, Okura's body vanished.
And so did the old man.{p}

Okura ended up listed as missing.
I couldn't exactly tell anyone the truth.
I mean, I'm the one who killed him.
Who the old man really was?
...I think he might've been a devil.
Sound crazy?{p}

But hey, you'd better watch yourself.
People like you, who get weirdly greedy, are the ones in the most danger.
If you ever meet some weird old man at a fair, don't go taking him up on anything.
You might think you're clever, but if he really is a devil, there's no way you can win.{p}Anyway, that's the end of my story.
Alright, time for the sixth one at last.{p}

He threw himself into his real business: loan-sharking.
Can you guess why?
So he could drag anyone who couldn't pay their interest into playing poker with him.
And the terms were something else, man.
If you beat Okura at poker, he'd wipe out your entire debt.
But a sweet deal always has a catch.
What do you think happened if you lost?
He said you had to hand over your soul when you died.
Everyone laughed.
Even if you lost, all you had to do was sign a note saying you'd hand over your soul when you died.
And on top of that, if you signed it, you got a nice little bonus: you could pay the loan back whenever you wanted.
In other words, for the people borrowing, it meant they basically never had to pay the money back.
Plenty of people went for it.
Though the straight-laced types wouldn't even look at it.{p}

As soon as they'd borrowed all they could, they'd challenge him to poker.
I mean, losing didn't cost them anything.
All they had to do was take the money and keep him company at poker.
Everybody was pretty casual about it.{p}

Okura never lost.
Well, the other side wasn't taking it seriously, so it was never much of a contest to begin with.
Everybody thought it was a laugh and wrote up contracts with the devil.
Okura looked happy, sitting in front of the pile of contracts he'd collected.{p}

It was a few days after that.
I'd stayed late at school on some errand.
Well, don't ask me why.
I've got my own stuff going on.
That's when I saw a figure in a corner of the classroom, huddled up like it was hiding.
I wondered who it was and went closer, and it turned out to be Okura.
"Okura."
Okura seemed startled by my voice.
But I was the one who got the shock.{p}

Because he was holding a knife.
When he turned around, he was frantically trying to hide something.
But he was too late.
I saw it.{p}What do you think I saw?

It was those contracts Okura had been getting everyone to sign.
And every single one had a photo of the signer on it. God knows where he got them.
There was a thick, worn-out old book, too.
Like some spellbook out of a fantasy story......
A spellbook?
He must've read the look on my face.{p}

Okura turned to face me.
His eyes were glittering.
"Well, you've seen it, so there's no helping it.
I'm going to trade these contracts to a devil and get even better at gambling.
Not just at school, either. I'm going to play for way bigger stakes!"
My body wouldn't move.
It was like something had me pinned in place.{p}

In the middle of it were three eyes, glowing with something evil.
Okura held up the contracts.
"I have here contracts pledging their souls."
This was bad!
I started to panic.
Okura meant it.
Once the deal was done, I'd probably be made an offering too.
I strained every muscle in my body.
"In exchange for these contracts, make me the greatest gambler in the world..."
My finger twitched.
And with that, I got control of my body back!{p}

It was now or never!
I stretched out my leg and scuffed the surface of the magic circle.
The powder flew up, and a piece of the circle was gone.
The next instant...{p}

"Gyaaaaaah☆"
A thick arm reached out, grabbed Okura, and dragged him straight into the mist.
In those few seconds, I hurried into the magic circle and redrew the broken part.
I didn't think I'd make it in time.
My heart nearly stopped.
Right after that, a voice came from the mist.{p}

"State thy wish..."
It was a deep, heavy voice.
I only had one wish.
"Go back where you came from, right now☆"
And the mist vanished.{p}

Once the relief hit, my legs gave out.
I couldn't move for a while.
Okura ended up listed as missing.
I couldn't exactly tell anyone the truth.
Well, he was an idiot, too.
He got what was coming to him.{p}Alright, that's the end of my story.
Time for the sixth one at last.{p}

You don't know......?
Are you even listening to me properly?
Whatever.
What I saw was those playing cards.{p}

Those playing cards.
Well, to be exact, not the cards themselves.
It was the half-skull woman drawn on the backs of the cards.
I couldn't believe my eyes.
Can you believe something like that?
That woman was crawling right out of the cards!
It was disgusting as hell.
And when I say woman, I mean just a head.
About the size of a ping-pong ball, and it looked kind of like a shrunken head.
And there was nothing below the neck.
Well, not nothing. Under the neck it was covered with tiny tentacle-like things, and they were all wriggling.
It moved those tentacles to walk.{p}

"Shindo! Don't look!"
Okura threw himself over them to hide them.
But there was no way he could hide them all.
And I was frozen stiff. I couldn't even move my eyes.
What do you think Okura was doing?{p}

He'd cut the pads of his fingers with the knife and was feeding them his blood.
Tiny women's heads were sucking on all five of Okura's fingers.
It was a grotesque sight.
Half of each face was a pure-white skull, right?
And yet the other half was smiling happily, like the blood tasted that good.
Eyes narrowed, half rolled back to the whites.
"These things can't live unless they eat people.
I'm out of time.
I need the souls of fifty-three people, no matter what!"
That's what Okura was screaming.
Maybe I was caught in those women's spell, because I couldn't move a single step.{p}

"Shindo! Please!
Die for me!"
The women's heads were greedily sucking on the fingers of Okura's left hand, right?
And he raised his right hand, the one gripping the knife, to swing it down at me.
That's when I came to my senses.
It felt like the women's spell had broken.
"Stop it!"{p}
I shoved Okura away as hard as I could.{p}

"Stop it!
I'll feed you, like I promised!
As long as I've got these contracts, you'll never run short of food!
The food isn't me......"
Okura couldn't get away anymore.{p}
The women were swimming happily in the pool of blood gurgling out of his belly.{p}

"Aaaaaaaaaargh!"
I let out a scream and ran for it like a madman.{p}

I don't remember what happened after that.
I killed Okura.
Even now, I can still see it.
...What happened to Okura after that, you ask?
Strangely enough, the bloodbath I saw in that classroom was gone without a trace, all cleaned up as if nothing had ever happened.
Okura was listed as missing.
He wasn't at home either.
He just vanished from in front of everyone, out of nowhere.
Though I'm the only one who knows the real reason.{p}

...But you know, lately I've been thinking.
Maybe it was all just an illusion.
At least let me believe that much.
Otherwise, I'm a murderer.
I don't know what those women were.
I bet those cards are their home.
And normally, they hide by plastering themselves flat on the backs of the cards.
Not that I have any idea where the cards or the contracts are now.
But what's going to happen to everyone who signed a contract back then?
Eating a soul... how do you even eat a soul?
Did Okura vanish from this world without even leaving a body because his soul got eaten?
If that really happened, and those women ran off with everybody's contracts...
I just can't stop thinking about it.
I mean, I'm one of the people who signed a contract too.
If those women are hunting down everyone who signed, then someday I'll...
Shindo had been staring at the floor, but suddenly he looked up.{p}

"Please, {a}!
Play me at cards, will you?
Whoever loses takes responsibility for the contract. That's the deal!"
{f:What the heck is that|What is that supposed to be}?
{f:I|I} was dumbfounded.
It was crazy for him to seriously think that way, and the deal didn't do anything for {f:me|me} either.
This was {f:ridiculous|absurd}.
But Shindo {f:seemed|looked} genuinely terrified.
Somehow, I kind of felt sorry for him.{p}What should I do?
Play him
Turn him down after all

"Okay, I'll do it."
When {f:I|I} nodded, Shindo's face lit up with joy.{p}

"Okay, then I'll take two cards out of my deck, an ace and a joker.
If you draw the joker, you lose.
If it's the ace, I lose.
Pick whichever one you want."{p}
Two cards were laid out in front of {f:me|me}.{p}Which one should I pick?
Left
Right

There was a tiny creature there, the size of a ping-pong ball.
Half of its head was a skull, and the woman's face on the other half was gazing happily at {f:me|me}.
Tentacles were writhing beneath the face.
No one but {f:me|me} had noticed it, but still.
{f:It was|It was} the woman from the cards.
{f:They really did come back|So they really came back}.
And {f:I|I}'d gone out of my way to throw myself in front of {f:those things|those women}, like a {f:total idiot|complete fool}.
Everything seemed to go dark before my eyes.{p}While {f:I|I} stood there silent, someone else spoke up in my place.
"Well then, time for the sixth story."{p}
{f:I|I} drew the ace.{p}

Shindo was so crushed it was almost pitiful.
Maybe he was more sensitive than he looked.
But {f:I|I} had no intention of playing again for him.
Sorry, Shindo, but I {f:had to|needed to} move things along.{p}"Well then, the sixth story, please."{p}

"{f:Sorry|I'm sorry}.
I'll have to say no."{p}

"I see... Yeah, of course."
Shindo's shoulders slumped.
He {f:seemed|looked} genuinely scared.
Sorry, but {f:I|I} had to hold back a laugh.
I mean, even if the skull women did show up, if they're that tiny, you could just stomp on {f:'em|them}.{p}

Half of the ping-pong-ball-sized head was a skull, and the other half was a woman's face.
{f:It was|It was} the woman from the cards.
The moment I saw its eyes, {f:I|I} realized my mistake.
There was no way anyone could fight back against them.
Those eyes.
I knew by instinct that if they fixed on me, I'd freeze up like a frog glared at by a snake.
And I understood why Shindo was so scared, too...
The woman scuttled away and disappeared from sight.{p}

But there were more of them.
What should I {f:do|do}?
Should I tell Shindo?
But what {f:would I do|would I do} if that made him angry and he lunged at me?
{f:I|I} agonized over it.
{f:They must have taken|It seems they took} that for awkwardness.
Someone spoke up in {f:my|my} place.{p}"Well... time for the last story."
{f:I|I}'d missed my chance, so all I could do was keep silent......{p}
